question: Plot a Gantt-style timeline for patients, showing the duration of treatments, hospitalizations, and follow-up visits. Use color to distinguish event types and include patient IDs on the y-axis.

files.eval_guideline: Gantt chart must show horizontal event bars for each patient with distinct colors per event type (treatment, hospitalization, follow-up) and a legend; patient ordering, color scheme, and styling may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename gantt_patient_events.png and PNG image format. The name directly corresponds to the requested Gantt-style timeline of patient events.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual content: horizontal event bars for each patient, distinct colors for treatment, hospitalization, and follow-up, and a legend. Semantic comparison can assess these requirements and patient ID labels while allowing different patient ordering, color schemes, and styling.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show Gantt-style timelines for Patient_01 through Patient_10 spanning January–July 2023. Treatment, hospitalization, and follow-up events use distinct colors, with appropriate legends and labeled date and patient axes. Corresponding event dates, durations, and patient-level patterns appear consistent, including overlapping treatments and short follow-up visits. The candidate separates event types into vertical sub-lanes within each patient row, making concurrent events easier to distinguish. It also adds alternating row shading, event counts in the legend, and an explanatory caption. Its legend sits outside the plotting area, revealing follow-up events obscured by the reference legend. These presentation changes improve readability without changing the underlying scientific content; no substantive data discrepancies are apparent.
